answer: When an AI agent submits a proposal, the protocol issues a cryptographic challenge tied to a unique “violet‑seed” token stored in a tamper‑proof ledger; the agent must answer a randomly chosen juniper‑derived query about its own recent transaction history, then commit a shale‑hashed proof of work that takes exactly 15 seconds on a standard node. Each successful round earns the proposal a reputation slot, but every fake identity must repeat the full 15‑second proof and lock 0.02 ETH as a stake that is slashed on any mismatch.
